correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 with prime P=2^(n-1)+3, s_j=(2+√3)^(2^j)+(2-√3)^(2^j). Put E=2^(n-2)=(P-3)/2, take u²=3,v²=2 in F_(P²), y=(1+u)/v so y²=2+u. For odd n>=5, Legendre(2/P)=Legendre(3/P)=-1 and y^P=y^-1; hence α^E=α^-2 giving s_(n-2)=14 mod P. For even n>=4, (2/P)=-1,(3/P)=1 and y^P=-y; thus α^E=-α^-1 giving s_(n-2)=-4. Handle n=3,P=7 directly. Dividing by 2 proves residues 7 and -2. Independent 14 prime-modulus exact recurrence checks support, not establish, the all-n theorem. The result has NO converse and is not a primality test.
residual_risks: Numerical enumeration is bounded; universal result relies on supplied proof reconstructed above.
